answers.a:
The latest major de jure change identified is the Government Service (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act No. 01 of 2026), which amended the Government Service Act, 2018 by substituting section 37A. The new section 37A creates special provisions on government employees’ conduct and punishment. It treats as misconduct disrupting government work such acts as disobeying lawful orders of superior authorities or government orders/circulars/instructions, obstructing their implementation, collectively abstaining from work without leave or reasonable cause, or preventing another government employee from attending work or performing duties. The listed penalties include demotion to a lower post or lower pay grade, compulsory retirement, and dismissal from service. It also establishes an expedited disciplinary process: a show-cause notice within 7 working days, formation of a three-member inquiry committee within 3 working days where proceedings continue, completion of inquiry within 14 working days with a possible one-time extension of up to 7 working days, recording failures by inquiry committee members in PMIS/dossiers, and appeal or presidential review within 30 working days depending on the authority issuing the punishment.

Before that, a major amendment was the Government Service (Amendment) Act, 2023 (Act No. 18 of 2023). It amended section 1 on the Act’s application, inserted subsection 1(4A), and made selected provisions of the Government Service Act applicable to employees of autonomous bodies, state-owned enterprises, and local government institutions—specifically sections 15 and 41–45. The 2023 amendment also made other textual amendments noted in the Act’s footnotes, including changes to cross-references and insertion of a requirement for consultation with the Commission in one provision.

The underlying framework is the Government Service Act, 2018, which came into force on 1 October 2019 under S.R.O. No. 305-Law/2019 dated 25 September 2019. It consolidated the statutory basis for government service by covering matters such as government control and jurisdiction over employees, merit and open competition in direct recruitment, promotion criteria, pay and benefits, leave, personnel records, welfare, and absorption of surplus employees. It also repealed several earlier laws, including laws on public servants’ retirement, service reorganization and conditions, special provisions for government servants, punctual attendance discipline, dismissal on conviction, and…

The snippets explicitly identify the Act’s commencement in 2019, the 2023 amendment, and the 2026 amendment replacing section 37A.
